analyst_view.overall: Early view: Arsenal lead the table with five straight league wins, the latest 1-0 over Hull through Martin Odegaard, but Bukayo Saka is out with a quad injury until December and Max Dowman serves the last game of a three-match ban. William Saliba is back after four months out. Newcastle are 12th under Matthias Jaissle, without Joelinton and Tino Livramento, and have won one of their last five.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean slightly lower: Arsenal's recent wins have been tight, they lose a main source of goals with Saka out, and Newcastle have scored once in their last two league games (0-1 against Everton, 1-1 at Fulham).

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners. Arsenal are likely to have most of the ball, and without Saka their attacks may lean more on crosses and set pieces, while Newcastle will push forward at home. The site's figure looks about right.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards. Newcastle's last game brought two late bookings for Schar and Dedic, and Jacob Ramsey returns from a one-match ban for two yellows against Everton. Until the referee is known, I keep the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.5 shots. I lean slightly lower: Arsenal have been controlling games without many chances at either end, as in the 1-0 over Hull, and Newcastle's attack has been thin, with one goal in two league games.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.8 shots on target. I lean a little lower: without Saka, Arsenal lose their most dangerous wide player, and Newcastle have managed one goal in two games, so neither side is likely to test the keeper often.
